# 213 — the north-star surface serves an agent zero facts. PR explainer (HIGH tier)

## Goal

`/?pool=<id>` is the north-star surface — both `pool_click` CTAs live there, and the estate points
**3,634** deep links at it. Fetched without JS it contains **zero** of the facts it is about: not the
APY, not the TVL, not the protocol, not the pool's own id. Everything appears only after
babel-standalone compiles and a DefiLlama fetch resolves.

This ships a **markdown twin** for each deep-linked pool at `pools/<id>.md`, served on
`Accept: text/markdown`, so one request returns the facts.

## The intuition

The fix was already 90% built and nobody had noticed. `tokens/usdc.html` server-renders all of these
facts for ~29 pools at once. The data, the generator, the trust rails and the formatting helpers all
exist — **only the per-pool address was missing**. So this item is mostly *addressing*, not computing,
which is why the diff is small in the places that matter.

## What changed, in reading order

**1. `audit-app.js` (+6 lines).** `extractDeepLinkPoolIds` is exported. It already existed as the one
canonical `?pool=` extractor (item 206 made it a shared helper precisely so a second regex would never
appear); this adds `generate-pool-pages.js` as its second consumer. No logic change.

**2. `generate-pool-pages.js` (new, 536 lines).** Scans the estate HTML with that extractor, resolves
each id against pool data, writes `pools/<id>.md`.

The load-bearing design decision is **where the data comes from**, because it is what makes fact parity
structural rather than disciplined:

- `data/pools-snapshot.json` is byte-for-byte the file the rendered page reads (`app.js:1123`/`:1260`,
  snapshot-first). It is also the **only** source carrying `kpis`, since `compute-kpis.js` runs *after*
  the CI SEO transient is written.
- So the generator prefers the snapshot per id, falling back to CI's `seo-pools.json` (the $1,000-floor
  transient the token/chain generators already consume) for the ~88% of deep-linked pools below the
  snapshot's $10M floor.
- Consequence, and it is the right one rather than merely the convenient one: a pool the page has no
  kpis for is a pool the twin has no kpis for. 207's honest "no rate history" line therefore appears in
  the twin in exactly the cases the page shows it — by construction, not by remembering to.

Trust rails are **imported, never re-typed** (`APY_SANITY_LIMIT`, `poolTotalApy`, `isAnomalousApy`,
`formatUsd`, `formatApy` from `generate-token-pages.js`). `PoolDetail.js` has no `module.exports` and is
out of scope per the spec, so its `getPoolTypeShared` / `getRiskAssessment` / persona / haircut logic is
**mirrored**, each block carrying an explicit `// mirror of PoolDetail.js:NNN` comment — and the drift
that mirroring invites is what `test_pool_twin_parity.js` exists to catch.

**3. `vercel.json` (+9 lines).** One redirect:

```json
{ "source": "/",
  "has": [ {"type":"header","key":"Accept","value":"(.*)text/markdown(.*)"},
           {"type":"query","key":"pool","value":"(?<poolId>[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-…-[0-9a-fA-F]{12})"} ],
  "destination": "/pools/:poolId.md", "permanent": false }
```

`redirects`, not `rewrites` — item 212's follow-up proved by live curl that Vercel's order is
`redirects → filesystem → rewrites`, which silently killed 212's original rewrite-based negotiation for
every page that actually had a twin. `permanent:false` (307) because the response varies by `Accept`.
The UUID-shaped `value` is load-bearing, not decorative: see the deviation below.

**4. `.github/workflows/sitemap-update.yml` (+8 lines).** Generator step placed **after** the chain-page
step — it needs both the freshly generated estate HTML and the kpis `compute-kpis.js` writes earlier in
the same job. Added to `push.paths` (so merging is itself the trigger) and to the commit step's
`git add`.

**5. Tests (+788 lines across three files).** `test_pool_twins.js` (36 assertions, plain),
`test_pool_twin_parity.js` (36 assertions, browser), `test_markdown_negotiation.js` (76 → 91).

## Deviations, both disclosed rather than buried

**1. An unknown UUID-shaped id 404s instead of falling through to HTML.** Static Vercel config cannot
express "serve the twin if it exists, else serve the app": a redirect cannot test file existence, and
the rewrite-based fallback would serve HTML under the `/(.*)\.md` rule's `Content-Type: text/markdown`
— a confidently-wrong body, the exact failure mode 212 exists to remove. What the UUID constraint buys
is real: a **malformed** id never redirects and genuinely does fall through to HTML. The criterion's
load-bearing half — never `llms.txt`, never the index, never another pool's twin — holds absolutely and
is asserted, not argued. Recorded as a partial pass.

**2. `pools/*.md` is not committed here.** Generating twins in this PR would pair them with CI-generated
HTML from a *different* DefiLlama fetch, breaking the fact-parity criterion on day one. Parity is
structural only when both come from the same run. Honest cost: between merge and that CI run,
`Accept: text/markdown` on `/?pool=` returns 404. Same trade as 212, same reason.

## The bug this build found in itself

The first cut implemented the rate note as **two** branches. The page's is a **three-tier
mutually-exclusive chain** (`PoolDetail.js:715-805` says so in its own comment), and the missing tier
was the honest one — item 071's `rateVolatilityNote`.

Blast radius, measured: **79 of 427** shipped twins (18.5%). The example is the twin the build agent
pasted into its own report as evidence of success — SOL-USDC / orca-dex, 21.24% now vs a 41.52% 30-day
mean. The page tells that visitor *"this pool's rate moves a lot"*; the twin was telling an agent
*"we've been tracking this pool's rate for 21 days"* — the steadiness framing, on the one pool where
the page deliberately withholds it.

That is the item's whole thesis inverted: a twin that drifts from the page is worse than no twin, and
this drift ran in the dishonest direction, in a format where nobody looks. Fixed; mutual exclusivity is
now swept across all 427 twins rather than assumed.

## Verification

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` @ `20e338756` plain lane (baseline) | **44 pass / 0 fail** |
| branch plain lane | **45 pass / 0 fail** |
| `test_pool_twins.js` | **36/36** |
| `test_pool_twin_parity.js` (real Chromium, 12 real pools) | **36/36, zero page errors** |
| `test_markdown_negotiation.js` | **91/91** (was 76) |
| `test_smoke.js` — both router paths | see LOG entry |

A first baseline run reported a pre-existing red; it was an artifact of a stale `origin/main`
remote-tracking ref pointing at a 3-day-old tree, caught because the same test passed on the branch and
failed on the "baseline" — an inconsistency a new generator cannot cause. Full write-up in
`213-notes.md`.

## Measurement

**None, and that is the honest answer, not a gap.** An agent that never executes JS cannot fire a
client-side event, and this stack has no server-log access. Recorded as a **capability bet**, exactly as
212 was. **No traffic or conversion effect is claimed in either direction.** The prerequisite for ever
measuring it is edge request logging by `Accept` header and user-agent — a separate item, and the honest
thing to file if anyone wants a number.

## Quiz

1. Why does the negotiation rule live in `redirects` rather than `rewrites`, and what did it cost to
   learn that?
2. The generator prefers `data/pools-snapshot.json` over CI's `seo-pools.json`. Give the two independent
   reasons, and say which one makes 207's honest line correct by construction.
3. A UUID-shaped `?pool=` id with no twin returns 404. Why can't static Vercel config do better, and
   what does the UUID constraint in the `has` value actually buy?
4. The rate-note bug affected 18.5% of twins. What made it a *trust* bug rather than a cosmetic one, and
   what feature of the build process caught it?
5. Why are `pools/*.md` deliberately absent from this PR, and what is the disclosed cost?
